notes.decision: Standard running header 'Of the Teacher' as throughout the Kephalaia codex.

Translated as 'has reckoned/has set' — qualitative perfect of ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon, account.' The verb takes a direct object (this rest, a remembrance) consistently across the page, fitting the ecclesiological semantic field of 'establishing/reckoning' a remembrance for the deceased catechumen. Also functions intransitively as 'be reckoned to' (line 4 pattern). Same root as ⲡⲣ̄ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'make remembrance' in glossary, here as an alternate verb of cultic-commemorative action.

Translated 'his four great gates' (preserving the ms glyph ⲋ as written). The ⲋ in this manuscript appears to function as a variant for ϭ; ⲛⲁⲋ = ⲛⲁϭ 'great' and ⲋⲣⲟ likely = ϭⲣⲟ, an unusual Lycopolitan/Manichaean form of ⲣⲟ 'gate.' Confirmed by line 17 'third gate (ⲋⲣⲟ)' as section-marker pointing to a soteriological/structural enumeration of four 'gates' through which the catechumen passes. Alternative reading 'victories' (= ϫⲣⲟ) less likely given the structural-enumerative function.
Parsed as ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ϩⲛ̄ ⲁⲓ ϭⲉ 'from these things, therefore' — closing the first section before the leer break. ⲁⲓ = Lyc. demonstrative 'these'; ϭⲉ = particle 'therefore.' Reading uncertain.

'The second' — Lycopolitan feminine ordinal ⲙⲁⲍ-ⲥⲛⲧⲉ marking the section division. Continued by 'The third (ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ)' at line 17, confirming the kephalaion's enumerative structure of four 'gates' (per line 7).

Translated 'for the man's portion' tentatively, reading ⲡⲁⲥ as Lyc. variant of ⲡⲁⲥⲉ 'half, share, portion.' The double-marker ⲙ̄ⲡⲁⲥ ⲙⲧⲣⲱⲙⲉ = 'for-his-portion of-the-man.' Could alternatively be a scribal redundancy or an unidentified pronominal form. Confidence low.

Translated 'she habitually washes' — habitual ϣⲁⲥ- + ⲭⲱⲃⲉ. The verb fits the soul-purification context (paired with ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ 'be purified'). Could alternatively be ϣⲱⲃⲉ 'change, exchange.' Going with the washing/cleansing register that matches the surrounding language of purification.

Translated 'his kin/relation' tentatively — fits the kinship-list context (father, mother, son, daughter, kinsman). The lexeme ⲥⲁⲩⲧ is unidentified; possibly Lyc. variant of ⲥⲟⲉⲓⲧ 'fame/report' or an unattested kinship-term. Confidence low.
Translated 'I marvel/am amazed' — ϯ-ⲱⲁⲡⲧ as 1sg present of a verb related to ϣⲡⲏⲣⲉ 'wonder.' The doubled ⲧ̄ⲧ may be scribal or a Lyc. orthographic feature.

Translated 'she habitually ripens forth' per accumulated glossary entry ϣⲃⲱⲛ 'ripening (tentative)' and the cosmological-soteriological context of the soul's gradual purification 'until this end.' The maturation/release sense fits the eschatological framework.
